q: Does Lactobacillus johnsonii 7409N31 carry the specific genomic markers used to select probiotic L. johnsonii strains (bile-salt hydrolase, class-II bacteriocins, exopolysaccharide biosynthesis clusters), and do those markers correlate with the health benefits Oh et al. imply for Hanwoo calves?
basis: Oh et al. 2023 (PMID 37970500) frame 7409N31 as a probiotic feed additive isolated from an 11-day-old Hanwoo calf and note enzymes for fibrous + non-fibrous carbohydrate hydrolysis, but neither the paper nor the deposited PATRIC/BV-BRC subsystems (30 Carbohydrate entries: di/oligo=12, C-1=9, amino sugars=7, mono=2) enumerate bile-salt hydrolase, bacteriocin, or EPS biosynthesis clusters. Probiotic strain-selection literature for L. johnsonii typically requires those markers.
next_steps: Run BLASTP of 7409N31 protein.faa against curated BSH (PF02275), class-II bacteriocin (BAGEL4), and EPS priming-glycosyltransferase profiles; cross-check against BV-BRC specialty-gene calls and antiSMASH v7 output; then compare presence/absence pattern with the L. johnsonii NCC533 / La1 reference genome and against reported in vivo Hanwoo calf outcomes.

q: Is 7409N31 unambiguously Lactobacillus johnsonii by modern taxonomic thresholds (ANI >= 95%, dDDH >= 70%) versus its sister species L. gasseri and L. acidophilus, given the well-known misclassification history inside the L. acidophilus complex?
basis: Oh et al. assign the species by 16S / older similarity criteria only; the paper does not report whole-genome ANI or dDDH against type strains. CP084221.1 is available and multiple type-strain genomes (L. johnsonii ATCC 33200T, L. gasseri ATCC 33323T, L. acidophilus ATCC 4356T) are public, so the boundary check is directly testable.
next_steps: Compute pyani ANIb + ANIm and skani ANI vs the three type-strain genomes; run TYGS/dDDH via type-strain-genome-server; also generate a core-genome tree with GTDB-Tk r220 to place 7409N31 in the current L. johnsonii clade; flag whether the >=95% ANI threshold is met against L. johnsonii ATCC 33200T and clearly separated (<95%) from L. gasseri / L. acidophilus.

q: Which mucin-adhesin and gut-colonization determinants are encoded in 7409N31, and how does that inventory compare across L. johnsonii strains that differ measurably in gut-persistence, particularly across host species (bovine calf vs pig vs mouse vs human)?
basis: The paper claims probiotic potential in Hanwoo calves without any adhesin or colonization-factor analysis. L. johnsonii persistence is known to depend on mucus-binding proteins (MUB / MucBP domain-containing surface proteins), aggregation-promoting factors, and pilus-like sortase-dependent structures, none of which are enumerated in the paper or in the current PATRIC feature set for genome_id 33959.595.
next_steps: Scan protein.faa with HMMER against Pfam MucBP (PF06458), Cna_B (PF05738), and LPXTG-anchor motifs; enumerate sortase (srtA-family) copies; cross-reference against a curated panel of L. johnsonii genomes from different hosts (NCC533 human, FI9785 chicken, N6.2 rat) and compute presence/absence + copy-number heatmap; correlate with any published colonization/persistence data per host.

q: Does 7409N31 encode a validated pathway for conjugated linoleic acid (CLA) biosynthesis, complete bile-acid metabolism (BSH + optional 7-alpha-dehydratase), GABA production (gadB/gadC), or CRISPR-linked immunomodulation loci, and are those inferences functionally supported or only sequence-inferred?
basis: L. johnsonii is repeatedly claimed in the literature to have CLA / bile / GABA / immunomodulatory activity, but Oh et al. do not enumerate any of these pathways for 7409N31. BV-BRC subsystem faceting in this replication only surfaced Carbohydrate metabolism (30 entries); Amino Acid / Fatty Acid / Cofactor subsystems were not queried and no functional assay is reported.
next_steps: Query BV-BRC subsystems for classes Fatty Acids/Amino Acids and Vitamins/Cofactors on genome_id 33959.595; run KofamScan/KEGG mapping for CLA-isomerase (myosin-cross-reactive antigen), BSH (choloylglycine hydrolase, EC 3.5.1.24), gadB/gadC glutamate decarboxylase, and CRISPR-Cas via CRISPRCasFinder; flag which pathways are gene-complete vs partial and note that functional (in vitro) validation remains a genuine open gap.

q: Does the deposited 7409N31 genome pass a modern probiotic safety assessment (EFSA QPS / FDA GRAS style): no transferable AMR determinants, no virulence factors, no mobilizable plasmids, and no problematic prophage cargo?
basis: This replication added abricate 1.4.0 screens across CARD, NCBI AMRFinder, ResFinder, VFDB, PlasmidFinder (DB rev 2026-Jul-03) and observed 0 hits in all five databases -- consistent with probiotic use, but the abricate default identity/coverage cutoffs may miss chromosomally-encoded intrinsic resistance and prophage-borne loci; and no prophage / integrative-element analysis was performed here or in the paper.
next_steps: Rerun AMRFinderPlus with --plus and lower thresholds; run RGI (CARD) in strict + loose modes; add hAMRonization to reconcile calls; run PHASTEST / PHASTER and geNomad for prophages / mobile elements; run MobileElementFinder for IS elements; produce an EFSA QPS-style safety dossier that enumerates any intrinsic vs acquired AMR, any incomplete virulence loci, and any prophage insertions relative to a reference L. johnsonii chromosome.
